project.name: waydroid-sensors
project.description: Host-side Android sensors HAL for Waydroid, fed by the Surface's Linux IIO accelerometer, so the Android container sees a real accelerometer and auto-rotate works. Reuses the upstream Waydroid gbinder/HIDL @1.0 ISensors layer (droidian/waydroid-sensors, GPL-3.0) verbatim and replaces only the data source with a direct /sys/bus/iio reader (src/code/SensorFW.cpp). Fully data-driven: IIO device name, poll rate and the mount matrix live here; the engine renders them into a KEY=VALUE conf the daemon reads at runtime — no values baked into the binary.

binder._doc: Waydroid's container hwservicemanager lives on this root-only node (/dev/binderfs/anbox-hwbinder, 250,6). service.cpp takes the device as argv[1]. CRITICAL: the system gbinder.d config only maps /dev/hwbinder, NOT /dev/anbox-hwbinder, so libgbinder has no protocol for it and add_service silently no-ops. We therefore generate our own gbinder.conf mapping this device to `protocol` and point the daemon at it via GBINDER_CONFIG_FILE.
binder.name: default

iio._doc: Accelerometer source. The daemon discovers the device by `name` under /sys/bus/iio/devices at runtime (device numbers are not stable across boots) and reads in_accel_scale itself. raw*scale -> m/s^2.
iio.name: accel_3d

mount._doc: Maps each Android axis to a raw IIO channel + sign (device mount matrix). Android frame: +X = screen right, +Y = screen top, +Z = out of screen; the axis pointing UP reads +9.81. SP8 values are resolved empirically via `build.sh calibrate` and committed here.

waydroid._doc_bootprops: Waydroid patched the Android framework (services.jar) to read waydroid.stub_sensors_hal AT BOOT: when 1 (the /vendor/waydroid.prop default), SensorService reports no sensors no matter what HAL is registered. We override it to 0 via Waydroid's waydroid_base.prop (applied at container start) so the framework loads sensors from our HAL. A runtime setprop is too late — only a boot-time override works.
waydroid._doc_stub: Waydroid boots an in-container STUB @1.0 ISensors (init service stub_service, process stub_process) that owns the HIDL name while stub_prop=1 and returns an empty list. Takeover order MUST be: stop the stub, (re)register our host daemon on the now-free name, then restart the Android framework (framework_restart) so sensorservice re-queries hwservicemanager and binds ours.

runtime._doc: The daemon must run as ROOT — the binder node /dev/binderfs/anbox-hwbinder is crw------- (root only) — so it is a SYSTEM service, not a user unit. Proper declarative home is a NixOS systemd.services entry in the Surface host flake (follow-up); build.sh install mirrors it imperatively for now (sudo).
